params.prompt: Original game HUD artwork for our own dark subterranean fantasy strategy game Kluftkrone. A coordinated tactile interface material family: rough hand-chiseled charcoal basalt, age-darkened bronze and oxidized copper inlays, sparse tiny amber mineral-lit abstract rune-like notches, restrained moss-gray mineral wear, deep soot-black recesses. Strong stepped geometric corners and bold carved edges. The clarity and chunky legibility of a 1990s fantasy strategy interface, newly crafted with rich modern material detail. Original geometric ornament only, no copied intellectual property, no existing game motifs. Flat frontal orthographic view directly perpendicular to the surface. No perspective, no camera tilt, no scene, no objects sitting on a table, no cast shadow outside the asset. Even studio-flat illumination with subtle shallow bevel shading in the material. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, words, labels, logo, watermark, symbols in the central writing area, or user-interface mockup. Create ONE SQUARE EDGE-TO-EDGE MENU PANEL TEXTURE suitable for CSS 9-slice scaling. The image itself IS the panel. A thick continuous carved basalt and bronze frame occupies the outer 18 percent of the width along EACH of all four sides; all four corners are fully present. The frame is flush with the canvas edges and reaches every image boundary: NO exterior background, NO padding, NO empty margin, NO freestanding box. Make the four corner ornaments compact, stepped, symmetric and contained within the 18-percent corner squares. Straight top, bottom, left and right edge bands should be consistent in thickness, quiet and repeatable, with balanced horizontal and vertical material. The inner 64-percent square is a single very dark quiet almost-black stone face, flat and unobstructed, with only faint fine grain so game menu text can be placed over it. Main outer frame: rough basalt slab, copper inner lip, a few tiny engraved amber notches restricted to the corners. No central decoration, no dividers, no buttons, no holes, no transparency, no lighting vignette. Read as one substantial carved HUD menu frame viewed perfectly straight-on.
